title: l'Arabesque (25 Etudes faciles, Op. 100, No. 2)
subtitle: Arabeske
trains: Quick 16th-note turn figures answered by a light eighth-note tag, alternating with a lyrical dotted-quarter melody, over a steady broken-chord left hand in A minor - finger agility and voicing a short melodic cell cleanly at a scherzando tempo.

provenance.author: Musicanyya practice material
provenance.basedOn: Burgmuller, 25 Etudes faciles et progressives, Op. 100, No. 2 "l'Arabesque" (public domain, published 1852). Every note and rhythm in both hands was checked against the exact pitch/duration/timing data in the Mutopia Project's public-domain MIDI rendering of its LilyPond edition (piece-info id 203, 25EF-02, typeset by Bas Wassink; source files 25EF-02.ly and 25EF-02.mid), read programmatically to avoid manual octave-placement error, then cross-checked measure-by-measure against the LilyPond source text itself (key A minor, 2/4, Allegro scherzando, quarter = 152, with a first-section repeat mm.3-11 and a second-section repeat mm.12-28, both with first/second endings, exactly as engraved here).
provenance.note: One deliberate change from the source: its closing flourish (written here at measure 31, 'risoluto') drops from the phrase's highest note straight down nearly two and a half octaves before the final four-note descent; we brought that landing up by one octave (to the E3-A2 register used here, mirroring the register of the piece's earlier phrases) so the largest one-hand leap stays inside this shelf's Intermediate cap, while keeping the same dramatic upward-then-down gesture and the same final cadence shape. Everything else is engraved exactly as the source has it, including the double repeat structure.
